answer: Yes, a fix was accepted. Robert Sanderson raised NEW ISSUE 475 on 2020-02-18 (thread t1325), pointing out that the E10 Transfer of Custody scope note contradicted itself: its first line said the class comprises 'transfers of physical custody of objects,' but a later paragraph implied a transfer could be of legal responsibility only, distinguished via P2 has type. He asked how legal-but-not-physical custody (e.g. an eBay sale, a pending house sale, an auction house that may only hold a photograph) could be modeled if E10 was strictly physical. As homework from SIG 47 (thread t1375, 2020-06-25), Sanderson drafted a fix: the first sentence should say the class comprises transfers of EITHER the physical custody OR the legal responsibility for physical custody, and the P2-has-type sentence should be reworded to say that when only ONE kind (legal OR physical, not both) is being documented, that distinction is expressed via P2 has type -- rather than implying physical was always the default. This went to an e-vote (thread t1394, Oct 2020, subject 'E-Vote: Change of Scope Note E10 Transfer of Custody (Issue 475)'). Sanderson's cover message explicitly named the reasoning: 'the scope note seemed to contain a contradiction since the first line indicated that the transfer of custody was of physical possession while the second paragraph indicated that it could be of physical possession OR only of legal custody,' and the fix would 'consistently express that the base line case is that BOTH physical and legal custody are transferred and in the case that it is only one or the other this would be expressed using the p2 has type property.' The vote passed unanimously YES (Sanderson, Martin Doerr, van Leusen, Oyvind Eide, Christian-Emil Ore, Pat Riva), with several voters attaching editorial caveats (missing verb, clearer wording on 'representative part' for physical possession, examples to be reviewed). George Bruseker incorporated these caveats into a revised scope note (2020-10-18) reading 'This class comprises transfers of the physical custody or the legal responsibility for the physical custody of objects,' with the P2-has-type sentence fixed to 'In the event that only a single kind of transfer of custody occurs, either the legal responsibility for the custody or the actual physical possession of the object but not both, this difference should be expressed using the property P2 has type.' The current ontology entry (search.py concept E10, v7.1.3) contains exactly this wording, and the episode for Issue 475 is marked [decided], confirming the fix was adopted as proposed.
notes: First query surfaced the whole issue cluster (t1325 new-issue report, t1375 homework draft, t1394 e-vote) on the first page of hybrid results, so no failed queries were needed. concept E10's current scope note text and its chronology entry marked [decided] independently corroborate that the e-vote's revised wording was actually adopted into the published standard, not just approved-in-principle.
